Physics hand-checked: eddy currents are induced currents flowing in closed loops in the body of a bulk conductor when the flux through it changes; useful in magnetic braking and the induction furnace, wasteful in transformer cores, which are laminated to reduce them.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.margin_note: First mark. Two phrases carry it: bulk conductor, and closed loops inside the body.
steps.why: The defining picture is a solid conductor, not a wire circuit: with no fixed path to follow, the induced current flows in closed loops inside the metal.
common_mistakes: Leaving out that the currents flow inside the BODY of a solid conductor. In a wire loop the same physics is just an induced current, not an eddy current.

recall.must_convey: That eddy currents are induced currents flowing in closed loops inside a bulk conductor when the flux through it changes.

steps.memory_tip: Bulk metal + changing flux = closed loops of current inside the metal.

steps.why: Naming one use and one loss shows both faces: the same opposing currents that brake a train also heat a transformer core for nothing.

recall.must_convey: That eddy currents are useful in braking and induction heating, and wasteful in transformer cores, which are laminated.
